docs.title: microbiome-analysis
docs.text: Reproducible microbiome analysis on real HMP-adjacent data: compositionality-aware differential abundance, diversity, ordination, and leakage-safe ML. Audited by tests and CI.

docs.title: What this project does
docs.text:
End-to-end pipeline that runs from real HMP-adjacent 16S data (122 samples x 122 genera) and produces:

  • Differential abundance with BH-FDR (Wilcoxon on CLR + ANCOM-BC-style)
  • Diversity analysis (richness, Shannon, Simpson; Bray-Curtis + Jaccard)
  • Ordination (PCoA on beta distance matrices)
  • PERMANOVA (group-difference test on community composition)
  • Leakage-safe ML (balanced accuracy, AUC, permutation-ranked features)

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: ```powershell pip install -e ".[dev,dashboard]" pytest -q python scripts/run_pipeline.py --source gmrepo --out results/real_sanity/ python scripts/run_ml.py streamlit run dashboard/app.py

docs.title: Data Provenance
docs.text: This document records exactly where the real dataset in this repository came from, how it was processed, and how to reproduce it. Anyone can follow these steps and obtain the same data/cache/_genus_raw.tsv.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
• BioProject: NCBI SRA, real 16S rRNA-seq gut metagenome samples
  • Number of runs: 124 (SRR41063392 – SRR41063515)
  • Organism: human gut metagenome (TaxID 749906)
  • Platform: Illumina MiSeq, paired-end
  • Sequencing strategy: 16S rRNA gene amplicon

docs.title: Processing pipeline
docs.text:
The raw data was processed with QIIME 2 (amplicon 2026.7):

  1. Import paired-end reads (SRA FASTQ → QIIME 2 artifact)
  2. Denoise with DADA2 (standard 16S parameters)
  3. Assign taxonomy with a Greengenes2 reference
  4. Collapse ASVs to genus rank → all-genus-table.qza
  5. Export to BIOM → convert to TSV

The final commands (from the working directory of the QIIME 2 environment):

```bash qiime tools export \ --input-path all-genus-table.qza \ --output-path genus-raw-export

biom convert \ -i genus-raw-export/feature-table.biom \ -o genus_raw.tsv \ --to-tsv

cp genus_raw.tsv data/cache/_genus_raw.tsv

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
We are explicit about what this does and does not claim.

  1. Compositional data. All DA runs on CLR unless rarefied explicitly. Absolute abundances cannot be recovered from 16S data alone.

  2. ANCOM-BC simplification. Our ancom_bc_da is a bias-corrected CLR + Welch t-test, not a reimplementation of the Bioconductor package. Cite Lin & Peddada (2020) for the method, not this code.

  3. No phylogenetic distances yet. UniFrac is planned for a future phase. Bray-Curtis and Jaccard are taxonomy-only.

  4. No batch correction. Metadata-level batch effects are not modeled.

  5. Single-cohort evaluation. The ML module is trained and tested on one cohort. Generalization to new cohorts is not validated here.

  6. Not for clinical decisions. This is a reproducible analysis toolkit and educational reference.

docs.title: Compositional transforms
docs.text:
Microbiome data is compositional: abundances are constrained to sum to a fixed total per sample (due to sequencing depth). We apply centered log-ratio (CLR) transform before any differential abundance test:

$$\text{clr}(x)i = \log(x_i + 0.5) - \frac{1}{N} \sum{j=1}^{N} \log(x_j + 0.5)$$

This makes relative differences interpretable and removes the depth-vs-abundance confounding.

docs.title: Differential abundance
docs.text:
Two independent methods:

  1. Wilcoxon rank-sum on CLR abundances. Non-parametric, robust to outliers. BH-FDR correction across genera at alpha = 0.05.
  2. ANCOM-BC-style bias-corrected CLR + Welch t. Bias correction subtracts the median CLR per taxon; effect size is mean CLR difference; W-rank combines |effect| and -log10(q).

Both report per-taxon: effect size, raw p, BH-adjusted q, direction, prevalence. Recomputed for each generation of the dataset.

docs.title: Alpha diversity
docs.text:
• Richness (observed OTUs): count of taxa with non-zero abundance
  • Shannon: $- \sum p_i \log(p_i)$
  • Simpson: $1 - \sum p_i^2$

Computed via scikit-bio alpha_diversity.

docs.title: Beta diversity
docs.text:
• Bray-Curtis: $\frac{\sum |a_i - b_i|}{\sum (a_i + b_i)}$
  • Jaccard: 1 - |A n B| / |A u B| (presence/absence)

Both produce symmetric N x N matrices with zero diagonal.

docs.title: Ordination
docs.text: PCoA (Principal Coordinates Analysis) via skbio.stats.ordination.pcoa. Projects the distance matrix into 2D for visualization. Reported variance explained: PC1 + PC2 percentages.

docs.title: PERMANOVA
docs.text: Permutation-based multivariate ANOVA on the distance matrix. Tests the null hypothesis "community composition does not differ by group", with 999 permutations for the p-value.

docs.title: Machine learning
docs.text:
Leakage-safe classification via sklearn Pipeline:

  1. CLR transform (fit-free)
  2. SelectKBest(f_classif, k=50) — fit on train fold only
  3. RandomForestClassifier(500 trees)

Critical: the feature selector is inside the Pipeline, so it sees only train-fold data during cross-validation. This is enforced by a leakage sanity test: on shuffled labels, balanced accuracy must be within 0.35-0.65 (chance for binary classification).

5-fold stratified CV. Metrics: balanced accuracy (handles class imbalance), AUC (for binary), confusion matrix per fold.

Feature importance: fit final model on all data, rank by feature_importances_ from the random forest. Reported top-20 genera.
